children.translated_text: by the power of their merit (<s>puṇya</s>), at the end went to the <s>Jina</s>-abode. [Avc 196]

children.text: tathābhūn magadhe deśe caityagarbhaṃ mahat saraḥ /
children.translated_text: Likewise, in the land of <s>Magadha</s>, there was a great lake containing a <s>caitya</s> within it,

children.text: śuddhāmbupūritaṃ padmakumudādipraśobhitam || 197 ||
children.translated_text: filled with pure water, adorned with lotuses, water-lilies, and the like. [Avc 197]

children.text: tatrarṣayaḥ saromadhye pratiṣṭhite jinālaye /
ahorātravrataṃ dhṛtvā satkṛtya vidhinārcayan // Avc_198 /
children.translated_text: observing the day-and-night vow, honored and worshipped it with due rites. [Avc 198]

children.text: tathā tair ṛṣibhiś caityaṃ pūjitaṃ tatsaraḥsthitāḥ /
children.translated_text: While the <s>caitya</s> was being worshipped by those <s>ṛṣis</s>, eight <s>Nāga</s>-maidens (<s>nāgakanyā</s>)

children.text: nāgakanyāḥ samīkṣyāṣṭau tadantikam upāśrayan || 199 ||
children.translated_text: dwelling in that lake, having observed [them], approached their vicinity. [Avc 199]
There the <s>ṛṣis</s> (seers), at the <s>Jina</s>-temple established in the middle of the lake,

children.text: tatra ta ṛsayas tāsāṃ saviṣaśvāsavāyubhiḥ /
children.translated_text: There, those <s>ṛṣis</s>, struck by the venomous breaths

children.text: prahatā viṣasaṃdigdhāḥ kṣaṇamātraṃ mumūrchire || 200 ||
children.translated_text: of those [<s>Nāga</s>-maidens], contaminated by poison, fell unconscious for a moment. [Avc 200]

children.text: tatas ta ṛṣayaḥ sarve kṣaṇāt prāptasucetanāḥ /
children.translated_text: Then all those <s>ṛṣis</s>, regaining consciousness in a moment,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā tāḥ samupāsīnā nāgakanyā ruṣāśapan || 201 ||
children.translated_text: seeing those <s>Nāga</s>-maidens seated nearby, cursed them in anger: [Avc 201]

children.text: are duṣṭāḥ supāpinyo yad yuṣmākaṃ viṣānalaiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Begone, wicked, most sinful ones! Since you have tormented us

children.text: tāpitāḥ smas tadapuṇyair yūyaṃ bhavata śambukāḥ || 202 ||
children.translated_text: with the fire of your venom — by the demerit of that, may you become snails (<s>śambuka</s>)!' [Avc 202]

children.text: iti tair ṛṣibhiḥ sarvaiḥ śāpitās ta bhayānvitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus cursed by all those <s>ṛṣis</s>, they, seized with fear,

children.text: sarvān ṛṣivarān natvā prārthayann evam ādarāt || 203 ||
children.translated_text: bowing to all the excellent seers, earnestly entreated them thus: [Avc 203]

children.text: namo vo 'stu mahāvijñāḥ kṣamadhvaṃ no 'parādhatām /
children.translated_text: 'Obeisance to you, O greatly wise ones! Forgive our offense!

children.text: tacchāpamocanopāyaṃ samupadeṣṭum arhatha || 204 ||
children.translated_text: Be pleased to teach us the means of release from that curse!' [Avc 204]

children.text: iti saṃprārthitaṃ tābhir niśamya te maharṣayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Hearing their entreaty, those great <s>ṛṣis</s>,

children.text: karuṇākrāntacittās tāḥ samālokyaivam abruvan || 205 ||
children.translated_text: their minds overcome with compassion, looking upon them, spoke thus: [Avc 205]

children.text: śṛṇudhvaṃ śambukā yūyam upāyaṃ śāpamuktaye /
children.translated_text: 'Listen, O snails! [Hear] the means for release from the curse.

children.text: asmābhir deśitaṃ śrutvā tathā carata sādaram || 206 ||
children.translated_text: Having heard what is taught by us, act accordingly with reverence: [Avc 206]

children.text: caityabimbaṃ samālambya tad anusmṛtya cetasā /
children.translated_text: Grasping the image of a <s>caitya</s> and remembering it in your minds,

children.text: sadā pradakṣiṇāṃ kṛtvā bhramitvā bhajatādṛtāḥ || 207 ||
children.translated_text: always performing circumambulation (<s>pradakṣiṇā</s>), wandering around it, worship it with devotion. [Avc 207]

children.text: tadā tatpuṇyabhāvena sarvapāpavimocitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, by the merit of that, freed from all sins,

children.text: pariśuddhāśayā bhadrā bhaviṣyatha nṛpātmajāḥ || 208 ||
children.translated_text: with purified intentions, O blessed ones, you shall become princesses. [Avc 208]

children.text: tadāpi hi tathā yūyaṃ caityasevāsamāhitāḥ /
children.translated_text: And then too, devoted to the service of the <s>caitya</s>,

children.text: saddharmasādhanaṃ kṛtvā prayāsyatha jinālayam || 209 ||
children.translated_text: having accomplished the practice of the true <s>Dharma</s>, you shall go to the <s>Jina</s>-abode. [Avc 209]'

children.text: iti tair ṛṣibhiḥ satyaṃ samādiṣṭaṃ niśamya tāḥ /
children.translated_text: Hearing the truthful instruction given by those <s>ṛṣis</s>,

children.text: śambukās tān ṛṣīn natvā tato 'gacchan nijālayam || 210 ||
children.translated_text: the snails, bowing to those seers, departed for their own dwelling. [Avc 210]

children.text: tatas tāḥ śambukāḥ sarvāḥ śālikṣetram upāsṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: Then all those snails, having gone to a rice field,

children.text: caityabimbam anusmṛtya praviceruḥ samantataḥ || 211 ||
children.translated_text: remembering the <s>caitya</s>-image, entered [it] from all sides. [Avc 211]

children.text: tatra vicchinnaśeṣāṃśaṃ śālistambaṃ vilokya tāḥ /
children.translated_text: There, seeing a rice-stalk stump with its remaining portion cut off,

children.text: caityākāraṃ samālambya saṃsmṛtvā sugatālayam || 212 ||
children.translated_text: grasping its <s>caitya</s>-like form, remembering the <s>Sugata</s>'s abode, [Avc 212]

children.text: sadā pradakṣiṇīkṛtya praṇatvā ca muhur muhuḥ /
children.translated_text: always circumambulating it, bowing again and again,

children.text: caityānusmṛtim ādhāya bhramitvā saṃprabhejire || 213 ||
children.translated_text: holding the remembrance of the <s>caitya</s> [in mind], they wandered around and worshipped. [Avc 213]

children.text: tatra tāḥ śambukāḥ sarvās tatpuṇyapariśodhitāḥ /
children.translated_text: There all those snails, purified by that merit,

children.text: tacchāpaparimuktyarthaṃ caityaṃ smṛtvā pracerire || 214 ||
children.translated_text: for the sake of release from that curse, remembering the <s>caitya</s>, moved about. [Avc 214]

children.text: kadā cit tatra matsyārthī dhīvaraḥ krūramānasaḥ /
children.translated_text: Once, a fisherman of cruel mind, seeking fish,

children.text: tatsarasi sthitān mīnān samāhartum upācarat || 215 ||
children.translated_text: came to that lake to catch the fish dwelling there. [Avc 215]

children.text: tatra sa dhīvaro dṛṣṭvā mīnāharaṇalālasaḥ /
children.translated_text: There that fisherman, seeing [the lake], eager to catch fish,

children.text: tīrastho jālam utkṣipya mīnān āhartum udyayau || 216 ||
children.translated_text: standing on the bank, cast his net and set about catching fish. [Avc 216]

children.text: tatra jāle pratikṣipte śambukā daivayogataḥ /
children.translated_text: When the net was cast there, by the working of fate,

children.text: sarvā api praviṣṭās tā na tu matsyo hi kaś cana || 217 ||
children.translated_text: all the snails entered it, but not a single fish. [Avc 217]

children.text: tataḥ sa jālam ākṛṣya pravisārya vilokayan /
children.translated_text: Then, pulling in the net and spreading it out to look,

children.text: dadarśa śambukā eva tatra matsyaṃ na kaṃ cana || 218 ||
children.translated_text: he saw only snails there — not a single fish. [Avc 218]

children.text: atha so 'prāptamatsyas tāḥ śambukā eva lubdhakaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then that greedy hunter, having obtained no fish, [took] only the snails,

children.text: ādāya parikhinnātmā svagṛhaṃ śanakair yayau || 219 ||
children.translated_text: and, weary in spirit, went slowly to his own house. [Avc 219]

children.text: tatra sa svagṛhaprāpto viṣannāsyo nirāśitaḥ /
children.translated_text: There, having arrived at his own house, dejected in face and without hope,

children.text: patnyāḥ sundarikāyās tāḥ śambukāḥ purato 'rpayat || 220 ||
children.translated_text: he presented those snails before his wife <s>Sundarikā</s>. [Avc 220]

children.text: tataḥ sa dhīvaro 'nyatra mīnān āhartum udyataḥ /
children.translated_text: Then that fisherman, intent on catching fish elsewhere,

children.text: bhuktvāhāraṃ yathāprāptaṃ jālam ādāya niryayau || 221 ||
children.translated_text: having eaten whatever food was at hand, took his net and went out. [Avc 221]

children.text: tataḥ sā dhīvarī dṛṣṭvā śambukās tāḥ puro 'rpitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Then that fisherwoman, seeing those snails placed before her,

children.text: bubhukṣitānupaśyantī niḥśvasanty evam ālapat || 222 ||
children.translated_text: looking at [her family] hungry, sighing, she spoke thus: [Avc 222]

children.text: hā kaṣṭaṃ kiṃ karomy adya bhojyaṃ kiṃ cin na me gṛhe /
children.translated_text: 'Alas, what wretchedness! What shall I do today? There is no food at all in my house.

children.text: kaḥ krīṇīyād imāḥ śuktīr jīveyaṃ katham atra hi || 223 ||
children.translated_text: Who would buy these snails? How shall I live?' [Avc 223]

children.text: tad imāḥ śambukāḥ sarvāḥ paktvā bhuñjyām ihādhunā /
children.translated_text: 'Then let me cook all these snails and eat them now;

children.text: etadāhāramātreṇa yāpayeyaṃ na cānyathā || 224 ||
children.translated_text: by this amount of food alone shall I sustain myself, and not otherwise.' [Avc 224]

children.text: iti niścitya sā nārī sarvās tāḥ śambukā api /
children.translated_text: Having thus resolved, that woman cooked all those snails

children.text: rasair yutāḥ svayaṃ paktvā bubhuje jīvitārthinī || 225 ||
children.translated_text: herself, with seasonings, and ate them, [merely] seeking to live. [Avc 225]

children.text: tatas tāḥ śambukāḥ sarvā daivayogānucāriṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then all those snails, following the course of destiny,

children.text: tasyā evodare yātā babhūvur ekapiṇḍitāḥ || 226 ||
children.translated_text: went into her very womb and became joined as one mass. [Avc 226]

children.text: tataḥ sāpannasattvābhūt pravṛddhagarbhabhāriṇī /
children.translated_text: Then she became pregnant, bearing an ever-growing weight of womb,

children.text: dine dine 'bhiruṣṭāṅgī svalpāhāraratā kṛśā || 227 ||
children.translated_text: day by day with swelling limbs, eating little, growing thin. [Avc 227]

children.text: tataḥ sā samaye 'sūta kanyakā hy aṣṭa sundarīḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, in due time, she gave birth to eight beautiful daughters,

children.text: ekanāḍīsamudbhūtāḥ samākārāḥ śubhāṃśikāḥ || 228 ||
children.translated_text: born from a single umbilical cord, of identical appearance and auspicious features. [Avc 228]

children.text: tatra sā jananī dṛṣṭvā hy aṣṭa tāḥ sundarīḥ śiśūḥ /
children.translated_text: There, that mother, seeing those eight beautiful infants,

children.text: samākārāḥ subhadrāṅgīḥ paśyantī vismayaṃ yayau || 229 ||
children.translated_text: of identical appearance and lovely limbs, was struck with wonder. [Avc 229]

children.text: tataḥ sa janakaḥ śrutvā jātā hy aṣṭa sutā iti /
children.translated_text: Then that father, hearing 'Eight daughters are born!',

children.text: vismitaḥ sahasopetya paśyaṃs tasthau suniścalaḥ || 230 ||
children.translated_text: astonished, quickly came and stood gazing, perfectly still. [Avc 230]

children.text: tatas tā dārikāḥ sarvās tayā mātrābhipālitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Then all those girls, nurtured by their mother,

children.text: pravardhitāḥ prapuṣṭāṅgā rurucuḥ paṅkajā iva || 231 ||
children.translated_text: grew up with well-nourished limbs, shining like lotuses. [Avc 231]

children.text: tatas tāḥ kanyakāḥ sarvāḥ pūrvapuṇyānubhāvikāḥ /
children.translated_text: Then all those girls, by the power of their former merit (<s>pūrvapuṇya</s>),

children.text: prītiviśrambhasaṃbuddhā dharmārthābhiratāśayāḥ || 232 ||
children.translated_text: awakened with joy and trust, their minds inclined toward <s>Dharma</s> and purpose. [Avc 232]

children.text: svakulavṛttisaṃtrastā dayārdrāḥ karuṇānvitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Distressed by the livelihood of their own caste, tender with compassion,

children.text: triratnadarśanotsāhasamanvitāḥ pracerire || 233 ||
children.translated_text: endowed with eagerness to behold the Three Jewels (<s>Triratna</s>), they went about. [Avc 233]

children.text: atha mātā samāhūya tāḥ sarvāḥ kanyakā api /
children.translated_text: Then the mother, summoning all those daughters,

children.text: matsyānāṃ vikrayārthena prairayat paṇyavīthikām || 234 ||
children.translated_text: sent them to the marketplace to sell fish. [Avc 234]

children.text: tatas tāḥ kanyakāḥ sarvā ādāya matsyabhājanam /
children.translated_text: Then all those girls, carrying a vessel of fish,

children.text: vikretuṃ saṃcarantyas tatpuramārgam upācaran || 235 ||
children.translated_text: walking about to sell them, came upon that city street. [Avc 235]

children.text: tatra tāḥ kramato gatvā mārgādūrasarittaṭe /
children.translated_text: There, going step by step, at a riverbank not far from the road,

children.text: kṣaṇaṃ viśramya sarvās tad ālokyaiva samāśrayan || 236 ||
children.translated_text: resting for a moment, they all looked about and took shelter. [Avc 236]

children.text: tatra tāsāṃ pradhāna yā jyeṣṭhā sā bhaginī sudhīḥ /
children.translated_text: There, the one who was foremost among them, the eldest sister, of keen intellect,

children.text: tāḥ sarvā bhaginīr dṛṣṭvā samāmantryaitad abravīt || 237 ||
children.translated_text: seeing all her sisters, addressing them, spoke thus: [Avc 237]

children.text: bhaginyo yat purāsmābhiḥ pātakaṃ dāruṇaṃ kṛtam /
children.translated_text: 'Sisters, the terrible sin that was formerly committed by us —

children.text: tenātra sāmprataṃ jātāś caṇḍālasya kule vayam || 238 ||
children.translated_text: because of that, we are now born in the family of a <s>Caṇḍāla</s> (outcaste). [Avc 238]

children.text: iti satyaṃ parijñāya viramya pāpakarmataḥ /
children.translated_text: Truly knowing this, refraining from sinful deeds,

children.text: dharmārthasādhane rantum arhāmahe vayaṃ sadā || 239 ||
children.translated_text: we ought always to delight in the practice of <s>Dharma</s> and [its] purpose. [Avc 239]

children.text: ihāpi cet tathāsmābhiḥ kriyate pāpasādhanam /
children.translated_text: If even here we continue to commit sinful deeds,

children.text: bhūyo 'pi narake lagnā duḥkhaṃ bhuktvā caremahi || 240 ||
children.translated_text: we shall again be stuck in hell and wander about, suffering. [Avc 240]

children.text: kadā vayaṃ tato muktāḥ sukhaṃ lapsyāmahe katham /
children.translated_text: When shall we be freed from that? How shall we attain happiness?

children.text: sadaivaṃ durgatau jātāḥ pāpeṣv eva caremahi || 241 ||
children.translated_text: Always born thus in unfortunate destinies (<s>durgati</s>), we would continue in sins alone. [Avc 241]

children.text: puṇyair vinā na mānuṣye janma saṃprapsyate kva cit /
children.translated_text: Without merit, birth as a human can never be obtained;

children.text: mānuṣye 'labhyamāne tu kutra dharme matiś caret || 242 ||
children.translated_text: and if a human birth is not obtained, where would the mind turn toward <s>Dharma</s>? [Avc 242]

children.text: vinā dharmamatiṃ bhadre caritum utsahet katham /
children.translated_text: Without the aspiration toward <s>Dharma</s>, O dear ones, how could one strive to practice virtue?

children.text: vinā bhadracariṃ loke sadgatiṃ katham āpnuyāt || 243 ||
children.translated_text: And without virtuous conduct, how could one attain a good destination (<s>sadgati</s>) in the world? [Avc 243]

children.text: sugatau ca sadā saukhyaṃ vinā dharmair na lapsyate /
children.translated_text: In a good destination, lasting happiness without <s>Dharma</s> is never obtained;

children.text: tasmād dharme matiṃ dhṛtvā caritavyaṃ śubhe sadā || 244 ||
children.translated_text: therefore, holding the mind firmly in <s>Dharma</s>, one should always practice what is auspicious. [Avc 244]

children.text: śubhena sadgatiṃ yātāḥ pāpena durgatiṃ gatāḥ /
children.translated_text: By merit one goes to a good destination; by sin one goes to an evil destination.

children.text: sukhaduḥkhāni saṃbhuktva bhramanti jantavo bhave /
children.translated_text: Having experienced happiness and suffering, beings wander in existence (<s>bhava</s>).

children.text: tad itaḥ sadgatiṃ prāptuṃ caremahi śubhe sadā || 245 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, let us always conduct ourselves in what is auspicious, so as to attain a good destination hereafter.

children.text: kiṃ cāpy etā vayaṃ sarvāś caṇḍālakulasaṃbhavāḥ /
children.translated_text: Moreover, all of us are born in a <s>caṇḍāla</s> (outcaste) family,

children.text: tat kathaṃ kulavṛttiṃ nu tyaktvā caremahi śubhe || 246 ||
children.translated_text: so how can we abandon our family trade and conduct ourselves in what is auspicious?

children.text: yad vayaṃ preritā mātrā matsyān vikrayituṃ khalu /
children.translated_text: Since we have been sent by our mother to sell fish,

children.text: tasmān mātur vaco 'śrutvā caremahy anyathā katham || 247 ||
children.translated_text: how can we disobey our mother's words and act otherwise?

children.text: yady atraitān avikrīya prakṣiptvā ca jalāśaye /
children.translated_text: If we do not sell these [fish] and instead throw them into the water,

children.text: riktahastāḥ kathaṃ gehe mātuḥ puro vrajemahi || 248 ||
children.translated_text: how shall we go home empty-handed before our mother?

children.text: yad bhogyaṃ no gṛhe nāsty etad eva hi jīvanam /
children.translated_text: Since there is nothing to eat in our house — this itself is our livelihood —

children.text: tat kiṃ sā jananī bhuñjyād vināhāraṃ na jīvati || 249 ||
children.translated_text: what then would our mother eat? Without food she cannot survive.

children.text: tad atra kiṃ kariṣyāmo dhig janma mānuṣe 'pi naḥ /
children.translated_text: So what shall we do here? Shame upon our birth even as humans!

children.text: varaṃ prāṇaparityāgaṃ na tu pāpārthasādhanam || 250 ||
children.translated_text: Better to give up one's life than to be an instrument for sinful purposes.

children.text: sarveṣām api jantūnām avaśyaṃ maraṇaṃ bhave /
children.translated_text: For all beings, death is certain in this world of existence;

children.text: iti matvātra samsāre vartayema śubhe sadā || 251 ||
children.translated_text: knowing this, let us always conduct ourselves in what is auspicious in this <s>saṃsāra</s> (cycle of existence).

children.text: tad atra jīvino matsyān prakṣipyaitāñ jalāśraye /
children.translated_text: Therefore, let us throw these living fish into the water here,

children.text: nirjīvān eva vikrīya mūlyaṃ mātur dadīmahi || 252 ||
children.translated_text: and selling only the dead ones, let us give the money to our mother.

children.text: yady evaṃ kriyate 'smābhiḥ papaṃ no vidyate na hi /
children.translated_text: If we act thus, there will be no sin for us at all,

children.text: kiṃ cit puṇyaṃ tu vidyeta tasmāt kuryāmahe tathā || 253 ||
children.translated_text: and some merit will be obtained — therefore let us do so.

children.text: ity atra me vacaḥ śrutvā tat kartum anumodata /
children.translated_text: Hearing my words here, agree to do this;

children.text: mātra śarikāviṣādatvaṃ kartum arhāmahe khalu || 254 ||
children.translated_text: we should indeed act so as not to cause sorrow like <s>Śārikā</s>'s to our mother.

children.text: etat tayā samākhyātaṃ śrutvā tāḥ paribodhitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Having heard what was told by her and being enlightened,

children.text: tathety abhyanumoditvā tad anukartum īṣire || 255 ||
children.translated_text: they approved saying 'so be it' and wished to act accordingly.

children.text: tatas tāḥ kanyakaḥ sarvās teṣāṃ ye jīvino jhaṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: Then all those girls took whichever fish were alive

children.text: tān sarvān sahasādāya prākṣipaṃs tatsarijjale || 256 ||
children.translated_text: and immediately seizing them all, threw them into the river water.

children.text: yāvanto nirgataprāṇās tān eva sakalān api /
children.translated_text: As many as were dead — all of those alone

children.text: ādāya tāḥ pure gatvā vyakrīṇanta yathocitam || 257 ||
children.translated_text: they took, and going to the city, sold them as was proper.

children.text: tatas tat paṇam ādāya sarvās tāḥ kanyakā mudā /
children.translated_text: Then, taking that money, all those girls joyfully

children.text: gṛham āgatya tan mūlyaṃ sarvaṃ mātuḥ samarpayan || 258 ||
children.translated_text: came home and offered all the proceeds to their mother.

children.text: evaṃ tayā jananyā tāḥ kanyakāḥ preritās tathā /
children.translated_text: Thus, those girls, sent by their mother in that manner,

children.text: sajīvāṃs tāñ jale kṣiptvā nirjīvaiḥ paṇam ādaduḥ || 259 ||
children.translated_text: threw the living ones into the water and earned money from the dead ones.

children.text: evaṃ tāḥ sarvadā nityaṃ kṛtvā bhuktvā vinoditāḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus they always did this and lived contentedly,

children.text: tadvṛttisaṃparitrastāḥ pāpaśaṅkā viṣedire || 260 ||
children.translated_text: yet troubled by that way of life, they grieved with apprehension of sin.

children.text: kasmiṃś cid divase sarvā mātrā tāḥ preritās tathā /
children.translated_text: On a certain day, all of them were again sent by their mother

children.text: mīnān vikretum ādāya nigame samupācaran || 261 ||
children.translated_text: to sell fish, and taking them, they proceeded to the marketplace.

children.text: tatrāsan daivayogāt te mīnāḥ sarve sajīvitāḥ /
children.translated_text: There, by the decree of fate, all the fish were alive;

children.text: tān sarvāñ jīvitān dṛṣṭvā sarvās tā vismayaṃ yayuḥ || 262 ||
children.translated_text: seeing all of them alive, all the girls were filled with wonder.

children.text: tatra tāḥ kanyakāḥ sarvāḥ samālokya parasparam /
children.translated_text: There, all those girls, looking at one another,

children.text: katham adyātra kuryāma ity uktvaivāvatasthire || 263 ||
children.translated_text: said 'What shall we do today?' and stood still.

children.text: tatra tāsāṃ pradhānā sā kanyā śuddhāśayā sudhīḥ /
children.translated_text: There, the chief among them, that girl of pure heart and good wisdom,

children.text: tāḥ sarvā bhaginīr dṛṣṭvā samāśvāsyaivam abravīt || 264 ||
children.translated_text: seeing all her sisters, consoled them and spoke thus:

children.text: bhaginyo yad ime mīnāḥ sarve 'pi jīvinaḥ khalu /
children.translated_text: "Sisters, since all these fish are indeed alive,

children.text: tat kathaṃ jīvino 'py atra vikrīṇīmahi sāṃpratam || 265 ||
children.translated_text: how can we sell them, being alive, now?

children.text: tasmāt sarvān imān matsyān prakṣiptvātra sarijjale /
children.translated_text: Therefore, let us throw all these fish into the river water here,

children.text: triratnasmaraṇaṃ kṛtvā tiṣṭhemātraikavāsaram || 266 ||
children.translated_text: and having performed <s>triratna-smaraṇa</s> (remembrance of the Three Jewels), let us remain for just this one day.

children.text: yadi gṛhe gamiṣyāmo riktahastā vinā paṇam /
children.translated_text: If we go home empty-handed without money,

children.text: mātā ruṣṭā parikruśya sarvā nas tāḍayet khalu || 267 ||
children.translated_text: our angry mother will surely scold and beat us all.

children.text: yac cāpy adya gṛhe kiṃ cid bhojyaṃ na vidyate kva cit /
children.translated_text: And also, today there is nothing to eat anywhere in the house;

children.text: tat kiṃ mātānnam aśnīyād bubhukṣitā caret krudhā || 268 ||
children.translated_text: what then — will our mother eat food? Hungry, she will rage in anger.

children.text: asmabhyaṃ cāpi kiṃ dadyād annaṃ pānaṃ ca kopitā /
children.translated_text: And what food or drink would she give to us when angered?

children.text: paribhāṣya muhur bālā api niṣkāsayed gṛhāt || 269 ||
children.translated_text: Scolding us girls repeatedly, she would even drive us out of the house.

children.text: tad adya kiṃ gṛhe gatvā sarvā apīha saṃgatāḥ /
children.translated_text: So what is the use of going home today? Let us all, gathered here,

children.text: triratnasmaraṇaṃ kṛtva tiṣṭhemahi dināntataḥ || 270 ||
children.translated_text: perform <s>triratna-smaraṇa</s> (remembrance of the Three Jewels) and remain until the end of the day."

children.text: etat tayoditaṃ śrutvā sarvās tā dārikā api /
children.translated_text: Hearing what she had said, all those girls too

children.text: tatheti saṃmataṃ kṛtvā sarvān mīnāñ jale 'kṣipan || 271 ||
children.translated_text: agreed saying 'so be it' and threw all the fish into the water.

children.text: tatra tāḥ kanyakāḥ sarvaḥ sarittaṭasamāśritāḥ /
children.translated_text: There, all those girls, having taken shelter on the riverbank,

children.text: triratnasmaraṇaṃ kṛtvā dhyātvā tasthuḥ samāhitāḥ || 272 ||
children.translated_text: performed <s>triratna-smaraṇa</s> (remembrance of the Three Jewels) and stood absorbed in meditation.

children.text: kena cit kathitaṃ tāsām etadvṛttiṃ niśamya sā /
children.translated_text: Someone reported their conduct; hearing of it, that

children.text: mātā krodhāgnisaṃtaptā vegāt tatra ruṣācarat || 273 ||
children.translated_text: mother, burning with the fire of anger, rushed there in fury.

children.text: tatra tā dārikāḥ sarvās tathā sthitā nirīkṣya sā /
children.translated_text: There, seeing all those girls standing thus,

children.text: jananī sahasopetya paribhāṣyaivam abravīt || 274 ||
children.translated_text: the mother quickly approached them, scolded them, and spoke as follows:

children.text: are re durbhagā bālāḥ kim evam iha saṃsthitāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Hey, hey, wretched girls! Why are you standing here like this?

children.text: pradoṣe 'pi gṛhe kena hetunā na samāgatāḥ || 275 ||
children.translated_text: Even at nightfall, for what reason have you not come home?

children.text: kim etān sakalān mīnān avikrīya vimuñcatha /
children.translated_text: Why have you released all these fish without selling them?

children.text: kiṃ cid annaṃ gṛhe nāsti tat kiṃ bhokṣyāmahe 'dhunā || 276 ||
children.translated_text: There is not a bit of food in the house — what shall we eat now?

children.text: kasyopadeśam ākarṇya kuladharmanirādarāḥ /
children.translated_text: Listening to whose instruction have you become disrespectful of the family trade?

children.text: pitror api vaco 'śrutvā krīḍathaivaṃ tad ucyatām || 277 ||
children.translated_text: Not heeding even your parents' words, you play around like this — speak up!"

children.text: evam ukte tayā mātrā sarvās tāḥ kanyakā api /
children.translated_text: When thus spoken to by their mother, all those girls

children.text: adhomukhasthitāḥ kiṃ cid api nocur viṣāditāḥ || 278 ||
children.translated_text: stood with faces cast down and, filled with sorrow, did not say anything at all.

children.text: tathā sthitāḥ svaputrīs tā dṛṣṭvā sā jananī ruṣā /
children.translated_text: Seeing her daughters standing thus, that mother in anger

children.text: sahasā samupākramya laguḍenābhyatāḍayat || 279 ||
children.translated_text: quickly advanced and beat them with a <s>laguḍa</s> (stick).

children.text: tataḥ sā jananī dṛṣṭvā sarvās tās trasitānanāḥ /
children.translated_text: Then that mother, seeing all of them with terrified faces,

children.text: bodhayitvā prayatnena nināya svagṛhe niśi || 280 ||
children.translated_text: roused them with effort and led them home at night.

children.text: tatra tāḥ kanyakāḥ sarvāḥ svagṛhe saṃsthitāḥ niśi /
children.translated_text: There, all those girls, staying in their house at night,

children.text: abhuktvaikāntam āśritya tasthuḥ smṛtvā munīśvaram || 281 ||
children.translated_text: without eating, took themselves to a secluded place and stood remembering the Lord of Sages.

children.text: tat paredyuś ca sā mātā hatvāpi jīvino jhaṣān /
children.translated_text: The next day, that mother, having killed even the living fish,

children.text: dattvā tān dārikās tāś ca vikrayāyairayat pure || 282 ||
children.translated_text: gave them to the girls and sent them to the city to sell.

children.text: mātrā tathā kṛtaṃ matvā sarvās tāḥ kanyakā api /
children.translated_text: Realizing what their mother had done, all those girls

children.text: tat kukarma iti dhyātvā tasthuḥ pāpaviṣāditāḥ || 283 ||
children.translated_text: reflected that this was a wicked deed and stood grieving over the sin.

children.text: tathā sthitāś ca tāḥ sarvā dṛṣṭvā sā jananī ruṣā /
children.translated_text: Seeing them all standing thus, that mother in anger

children.text: bahuśaḥ paribhāṣitvā pratāḍya prairayat pure || 284 ||
children.translated_text: scolded them profusely, beat them, and sent them off to the city.

children.text: tatas tā dārikāḥ sarvās tattāḍanarujānvitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Then all those girls, suffering from the pain of her beating,

children.text: viṣaṇṇās tāñ jhaṣān dhṛtvā vikretuṃ niryayuḥ śanaiḥ || 285 ||
children.translated_text: distressed, took those fish and slowly went out to sell them.

children.text: tatas tā nirgatāḥ sarvās tanmārgasarasītaṭe /
children.translated_text: Then, all of them having gone out, at the bank of a stream along the road,

children.text: mātṛtāḍanaduḥkhārtā viśramya kṣaṇam āśrayan || 286 ||
children.translated_text: pained by the suffering of their mother's beating, they rested for a moment.

children.text: tatra tāḥ kanyakāḥ sarvās tatpāpapariśodhane /
children.translated_text: There, all those girls, for the purification of that sin,

children.text: triratnasmaraṇaṃ kṛtvā tasthur dhyānasamāhitāḥ || 287 ||
children.translated_text: performed <s>triratna-smaraṇa</s> (remembrance of the Three Jewels) and stood absorbed in meditation.

children.text: tatpuṇyapariśuddhās tā vālukābhiḥ pṛthak pṛthak /
children.translated_text: Purified by that merit, each one separately with sand

children.text: caityaṃ nirmāya satkṛtya pratiṣṭhāpya pramoditāḥ || 288 ||
children.translated_text: built a <s>caitya</s> (stūpa), consecrated it reverently, and rejoiced.

children.text: tatrotpannāni puṣpāṇi phalāni ca samantataḥ /
children.translated_text: Taking the flowers and fruits that had grown there all around,

children.text: ādāya taiḥ phalaiḥ puṣpaiḥ svasvacaityaṃ samarcayan || 289 ||
children.translated_text: they worshipped each of their own <s>caityas</s> (stūpas) with those fruits and flowers.

children.text: tatas tāḥ prāñjaliṃ dhṛtvā kṛtvā pradakṣiṇāni ca /
children.translated_text: Then, holding their palms joined in reverence and performing <s>pradakṣiṇā</s> (circumambulation),

children.text: aṣṭāṅgapraṇatiṃ kṛtvā tasthur dhyānasamāhitāḥ || 290 ||
children.translated_text: and performing <s>aṣṭāṅga-praṇati</s> (eight-limbed prostration), they stood absorbed in meditation.

children.text: taddinānte 'pi tāḥ sarvā gṛhe naivāgatā iti /
children.translated_text: Since even at the end of that day all of them had not come home,

children.text: mātā vicintya bhartāraṃ sahasā caivam abravīt || 291 ||
children.translated_text: the mother, worrying, quickly spoke thus to her husband:

children.text: svāmiṃs tā dārikāḥ sarvā adyāpi nāgatā gṛhe /
children.translated_text: "Husband, all those girls have not come home even today;

children.text: kutra gatā iti draṣṭuṃ gaccha tvaṃ sahasānaya || 292 ||
children.translated_text: go and see where they have gone, and bring them back at once."

children.text: etat patnyoditaṃ śrutvā sa caṇḍālaḥ prakopitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Hearing what his wife said, that <s>caṇḍāla</s> (outcaste), enraged,

children.text: sahasā tatsarastīre gacchan sarvā dadarśa tāḥ || 293 ||
children.translated_text: went quickly to the bank of that stream and saw them all.

children.text: tatra tāś caityam abhyarcya sthitāḥ sarvā vilokya saḥ /
children.translated_text: There, seeing them all standing having worshipped the <s>caitya</s> (stūpa),

children.text: pitātikopasaṃtaptaḥ sahasā saṃmukho 'carat || 294 ||
children.translated_text: the father, burning with extreme anger, quickly approached them.

children.text: tatra tāḥ kanyakāḥ sarvā dṛṣṭvā taṃ saṃmukhāgatam /
children.translated_text: There, all those girls, seeing him come toward them,

children.text: krodhasaṃtaptaraktākṣaṃ tasthur dhyānasamāhitāḥ || 295 ||
children.translated_text: his eyes reddened with rage, stood firm, absorbed in meditation.

children.text: tathā sthitāḥ sa ālokya sarvās tāḥ svātmajā api /
children.translated_text: Seeing all his own daughters standing thus,

children.text: nirdayo bahudhā bhartsya laguḍenāpy atāḍayat || 296 ||
children.translated_text: the merciless [father] threatened them in many ways and beat them with a <s>laguḍa</s> (stick).

children.text: tathātitāḍitāḥ sarvā api tā na vicerire /
children.translated_text: Though severely beaten, all of them did not stir,

children.text: tatpāpatrasitā eva tasthur dhyānasamāhitāḥ || 297 ||
children.translated_text: frightened only of that sin, they stood absorbed in meditation.

children.text: tataḥ sa janakaḥ krūraḥ saṃtāḍya paribhāṣya ca /
children.translated_text: Then that cruel father, having beaten and scolded them,

children.text: sarvā ādāya tān mīnān sahasā tatpure 'carat || 298 ||
children.translated_text: took all those fish and immediately went to the city.

children.text: tatra vikrīya tān mīnān annam ādāya satvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: There, having sold those fish and quickly taking food,

children.text: gṛhe patnyāḥ puro gatvā tac caritraṃ nyavedayat || 299 ||
children.translated_text: he went home before his wife and reported what had happened.

children.text: tatra tattāḍanodbhūtaduḥsahavedanāturāḥ /
children.translated_text: There, those [girls], afflicted by the unbearable pain arising from that beating,

children.text: bhuvy āvartya rudantyas tāḥ sarvās tasthur vimūrchitāḥ || 300 ||
children.translated_text: rolling on the ground and weeping, they all stood there, having fainted.

children.text: tadantikagireḥ sānau niṣaṇṇaḥ karuṇānidhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Seated on the peak of a nearby mountain, the treasury of compassion,

children.text: pratyekabuddha ātmajñaḥ śuśrāva tadvilāpitam || 301 ||
children.translated_text: A <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> (solitary awakened one), a knower of the self, heard their lamentation. (301)

children.text: tatra sa kṛpayā dṛṣṭyā vilokayan samantataḥ /
children.translated_text: There, with a compassionate gaze, looking all around,

children.text: tāḥ sarvā vedanākrāntāḥ samaikṣata vimūrchitāḥ || 302 ||
children.translated_text: he saw them all stricken by pain and fallen unconscious. (302)

children.text: tataḥ pratyekabuddhaḥ sa kāruṇyacoditaḥ kṛtī /
children.translated_text: Then that <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, driven by compassion, accomplished one,

children.text: taddeśaṃ sahasopetya tasthau sudhākarotsṛjan || 303 ||
children.translated_text: swiftly approached that place and stood there, emitting a stream of nectar. (303)

children.text: sarvās tās tatsudhāraśmiparispṛṣṭāḥ sukhānvitāḥ /
children.translated_text: All of them, touched by the rays of his nectar, filled with happiness,

children.text: saṃprāptacetanāḥ sarvāḥ prādrākṣus taṃ yatīśvaram || 304 ||
children.translated_text: having regained consciousness, all beheld that lord of ascetics. (304)

children.text: tatas tās taṃ muniṃ dṛṣṭvā vismayākrāntamānasāḥ /
children.translated_text: Then they, having seen that sage, their minds overcome with wonder,

children.text: ko 'yaṃ munir iti dhyātvā sarvās tasthuḥ pramoditāḥ || 305 ||
children.translated_text: thinking 'Who is this sage?' — all stood delighted. (305)

children.text: tatas tāsāṃ pradhānā yā bhaginī sā vicakṣaṇā /
children.translated_text: Then she who was the eldest among those sisters, that discerning one,

children.text: tāḥ sarvā bhaginīr dṛṣṭvā samāmantryaivam abravīt || 306 ||
children.translated_text: having seen all her sisters, calling them together, spoke thus: (306)

children.text: dhanyā vayaṃ tad adya smo yad ayaṃ saugato muniḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Fortunate are we today, indeed, that this sage of the <s>Sugata</s>'s [lineage],

children.text: kṛpayāsmān samuddhartuṃ svayam eva samāgataḥ || 307 ||
children.translated_text: has himself come to rescue us out of compassion! (307)

children.text: yady ayaṃ nāgato buddhaḥ sudhāraśmir dayānidhiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Had this <s>Buddha</s>, this treasury of compassion with his nectar-rays, not come,

children.text: nistrāṇā vayam atraiva sarvā mṛtyuṃ vrajemahi || 308 ||
children.translated_text: we, without any savior, would all have died right here. (308)

children.text: dhanyo 'yaṃ sugato nāthaḥ sarvasattvānukampakaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Blessed is this <s>Sugata</s>, the protector, who has compassion for all beings;

children.text: ko hy asti trijagalloke buddhād anyo hitaṃkaraḥ || 309 ||
children.translated_text: for who else in the triple world is a benefactor other than the <s>Buddha</s>? (309)

children.text: buddha eva jagacchāstā sarvabhadrārthasādhakaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The <s>Buddha</s> alone is the teacher of the world, the accomplisher of all auspicious aims,

children.text: durgatitrāyako nāthaḥ sadgater mārgadarśakaḥ || 310 ||
children.translated_text: the protector who saves from bad destinies, the guide to the path of good destiny. (310)

children.text: tad etasya vayaṃ sarvāḥ sarvadā śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore let us all, at all times, go for refuge to him;

children.text: satkṛtya śraddhayā bhaktya yathāśakti bhajemahi || 311 ||
children.translated_text: with honor, faith, and devotion, let us worship him to the best of our ability. (311)

children.text: tato nūnaṃ vayaṃ sarvāḥ sarvapāpavimocitāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Then surely we all, freed from all sins,

children.text: pariśuddhatrikāyā hi sadgatiṃ ca vrajemahi || 312 ||
children.translated_text: with our three doors purified, shall proceed to a good destiny. (312)'

children.text: etat tayā samākhyātaṃ śrutvā tāḥ paribodhitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Having heard what she proclaimed, they were awakened;

children.text: sarvā api munes tasya tathā bhaktuṃ samīṣire || 313 ||
children.translated_text: all of them also resolved to worship that sage in the same way. (313)

children.text: tatas tāḥ kanyakāḥ sarvāḥ śraddhābhaktisamanvitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Then all those maidens, endowed with faith and devotion,

children.text: yathāśakti munes tasya satkāraiḥ prābhajan mudā || 314 ||
children.translated_text: joyfully worshipped that sage with honors to the best of their ability. (314)

children.text: tatas tāḥ śaraṇaṃ gatvā kṛtāñjalipuṭā mudā /
children.translated_text: Then, having gone for refuge, with palms joined in joy,

children.text: tridhā pradakṣiṇīkṛtya natvaivaṃ prārthayaṃs tathā || 315 ||
children.translated_text: having circumambulated him three times, bowing down, they thus prayed: (315)

children.text: bhagavan nātha sarvajña bhavatāṃ sarvadā vayam /
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Bhagavān</s>, protector, omniscient one! We are always

children.text: śaraṇasthā yathādeśam icchāmaś carituṃ tathā || 316 ||
children.translated_text: in your refuge and wish to practice according to your instruction. (316)

children.text: tad bhavān kṛpayā dṛṣṭyā paśyann asmān suduḥkhitāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, looking upon us who are greatly suffering, with a compassionate gaze,

children.text: sarvadāpi tathā sarvāḥ paritrātuṃ samarhati || 317 ||
children.translated_text: you are worthy of always protecting us all in every way. (317)

children.text: nānyo no vidyate trātā nātho mitraṃ suhṛd guruḥ /
children.translated_text: 'No other savior, protector, friend, companion, or teacher exists for us;

children.text: bhavān eva guruḥ śāstā saddharmadeśakaḥ prabhuḥ || 318 ||
children.translated_text: you alone are our teacher, master, preacher of the true <s>Dharma</s>, our lord. (318)

children.text: tad asmān duḥkhinīḥ sarvāḥ saṃpaśyan karuṇādṛśā /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, looking upon all of us who are suffering with a compassionate eye,

children.text: bodhimārge pratiṣṭhāpya sadaivaṃ trātum arhati || 319 ||
children.translated_text: having established us on the path of awakening (<s>bodhimārga</s>), you are worthy of always protecting us thus. (319)'

children.text: etat saṃprārthitaṃ tābhiḥ śrutvā so 'rhan mahāmatiḥ /
children.translated_text: Having heard this prayer of theirs, that <s>Arhat</s> of great wisdom,

children.text: pratyekasugato jñātvā tāsāṃ karmavipākatām || 320 ||
children.translated_text: the solitary <s>Sugata</s> (<s>Pratyekabuddha</s>), knowing the ripening of their <s>karma</s> — (320)

children.text: tata ākāśa utplutya sthitvā vahnir ivojjvalan /
children.translated_text: then, leaping into the sky and standing there, blazing like fire,

children.text: taccittasaṃvinodārthaṃ prātihāryam adarśayat || 321 ||
children.translated_text: he displayed a miracle to delight their minds. (321)

children.text: tasyaitat prātihāryaṃ tāḥ sarvā dṛṣṭvā savismayāḥ /
children.translated_text: Seeing that miracle of his, all of them filled with wonder,

children.text: suprasannamukhāmbhojāḥ sulabdhabodhimānasāḥ || 322 ||
children.translated_text: with lotus-faces well-pleased, their minds having gained awakening — (322)

children.text: tatra pradakṣiṇīkṛtya kṛtāñjalipuṭā mudā /
children.translated_text: there, having circumambulated him, with palms joined in joy,

children.text: aṣṭāṅgapraṇatiṃ kṛtvā bodhipraṇidhim ādadhuḥ || 323 ||
children.translated_text: having made a prostration with eight limbs, they undertook the vow for awakening (<s>bodhipraṇidhi</s>). (323)

children.text: yad asmābhir muner asya satkṛtiḥ prakṛtā mudā /
children.translated_text: 'By the worship that we have joyfully performed for this sage —

children.text: etatpuṇyavipākena labdhvā ca janma sadgatau || 324 ||
children.translated_text: by the ripening of this merit, having obtained birth in a good destiny, (324)

children.text: svaparātmahitaṃ kṛtvā sarvatrāpi śubhāni ca /
children.translated_text: 'having accomplished benefit for ourselves and others, and auspicious deeds everywhere,

children.text: īdṛkpratyekasaṃbodhiṃ labdhvā vrajema nirvṛtim || 325 ||
children.translated_text: may we, having attained such <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> awakening, proceed to <s>nirvāṇa</s>! (325)'

children.text: evaṃ tāḥ kanyakāḥ sarvāḥ praṇidhāya prasāditāḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus all those maidens, having made their vow and being pleased,

children.text: tam eva sugataṃ natvā tasthur dhyānasamāhitāḥ || 326 ||
children.translated_text: bowing to that very <s>Sugata</s>, remained absorbed in meditation. (326)

children.text: evaṃ hṛdbhāvitaṃ tāsāṃ matvā sa sugatas tataḥ /
children.translated_text: Knowing that their hearts were thus cultivated, the <s>Sugata</s> then,

children.text: ākāśāt sahasopetya tā evaṃ samupādiśat || 327 ||
children.translated_text: swiftly descending from the sky, instructed them thus: (327)

children.text: bhaginyaḥ saṃprasīdadhvaṃ yad itaḥ saptame 'hani /
children.translated_text: 'Sisters, be at peace! On the seventh day from now,

children.text: sarvā yūyaṃ subhāvinyaḥ samaṃ kālaṃ gamiṣyatha || 328 ||
children.translated_text: all of you, good-natured ones, will die together at the same time. (328)

children.text: tato rājakule janma vārāṇasyāṃ śubhāṃśikāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Then, born in a royal family at <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, of auspicious portions,

children.text: labdhvā yūyaṃ samācārāḥ sarvāḥ śubhe cariṣyatha || 329 ||
children.translated_text: you, of good conduct, will all practice what is auspicious. (329)

children.text: tatra yūyaṃ samālokya saṃsāraṃ kleśasaṃkulam /
children.translated_text: 'There, perceiving <s>saṃsāra</s> filled with afflictions,

children.text: sarvān parigrahāṃs tyaktvā tapovane ramiṣyatha || 330 ||
children.translated_text: abandoning all possessions, you will delight in the forest of austerities. (330)

children.text: tatrāpi ca triratnāni smṛtvā sadā samāhitāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'And there too, remembering the Three Jewels (<s>Triratna</s>) always, concentrated,

children.text: pratyekāṃ bodhim āsādya nirvṛtipadam āpsyatha || 331 ||
children.translated_text: having attained <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> awakening, you will reach the state of <s>nirvṛti</s> (peace). (331)

children.text: etan matvā bhaginyo 'tra sarvā yūyaṃ samāhitāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Knowing this, sisters, all of you, concentrated,

children.text: triratnabhajanaṃ kṛtvā carata sarvadā śubhe || 332 ||
children.translated_text: having worshipped the Three Jewels, always practice what is auspicious. (332)'

children.text: etad evam upādiśya sa pratyekajinas tataḥ /
children.translated_text: Having thus instructed them, that solitary <s>Jina</s>,

children.text: bhāsayan khaṃ samutplutya svāśramaṃ sahasā yayau || 333 ||
children.translated_text: illuminating the sky, leaping up, swiftly went to his hermitage. (333)

children.text: tam ākāśagataṃ dṛṣṭvā sarvās tāḥ kanyakā mudā /
children.translated_text: Seeing him gone into the sky, all those maidens joyfully,

children.text: praṇatvā suprasādinyaś cireṇa svālaye 'caran || 334 ||
children.translated_text: bowing down, well-pleased, after a while went to their own dwellings. (334)

children.text: tatra tāś caityam abhyarcya sthitāḥ saptadine mṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: There, having worshipped a <s>caitya</s>, they remained for seven days and died;

children.text: vārāṇasyāṃ kṛke rajñaḥ sutā āsan samānikāḥ || 335 ||
children.translated_text: they were born as daughters of King <s>Kṛke</s> at <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, all of equal [age]. (335)

children.text: tāsaṃ yā bhaginī jyeṣṭhā vratīti pratiśrutā /
children.translated_text: She who was the eldest sister was known as <s>Vratī</s> (the Vow-keeper);

children.text: dvitīyā dharmavatī khyātā tṛtīyā śubhamañjarī || 336 ||
children.translated_text: the second was called <s>Dharmavatī</s>, the third <s>Śubhamañjarī</s>. (336)

children.text: caturthī dhīmatī nāmnā pañcamī netramañjarī /
children.translated_text: The fourth was named <s>Dhīmatī</s>, the fifth <s>Netramañjarī</s>;

children.text: ṣaṣṭhī ca śrimatī khyātā saptamī ca madaṃjahā || 337 ||
children.translated_text: the sixth was known as <s>Śrīmatī</s>, and the seventh <s>Madaṃjahā</s> (Destroyer of Pride). (337)

children.text: aṣṭamī ratnamālākhyā ity etā aṣṭakanyakāḥ /
children.translated_text: The eighth was called <s>Ratnamālā</s> (Jewel Garland) — these eight maidens,

children.text: sujātā nṛpateḥ putryaḥ samācārāḥ samāśayāḥ || 338 ||
children.translated_text: well-born daughters of the king, were of good conduct and of like aspirations. (338)

children.text: {E adds the following after vs. 338 and continues from 339
children.translated_text: {Manuscript E adds the following after verse 338 and continues from 339:

children.text: tatra tāḥ dharmavatyādi saptakanyā śubhecarāḥ /
children.translated_text: There those seven maidens beginning with <s>Dharmavatī</s>, practitioners of virtue,

children.text: kleśavyākulasaṃsāram ity ālokya parigrahān /
children.translated_text: perceiving <s>saṃsāra</s> as full of afflictions, [abandoned] their possessions —

children.text: svān svān sarvān parityaktvā sarvāḥ tapovanaṃ yayuḥ // Avc_338* //
children.translated_text: each abandoning all their own, all of them went to the forest of austerities. (338*)

children.text: tatrāpi ca triratnāni sadā smṛtvā samāhitāḥ /
children.translated_text: And there too, remembering the Three Jewels always, concentrated,

children.text: pratyekāṃ bodhim āsādya nirvṛtiṃ tāḥ samāyayuḥ // Avc_338** //
children.translated_text: having attained <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> awakening, they reached <s>nirvṛti</s>. (338**)

children.text: tāsaṃ jyeṣṭhā svasā yā tat vrataṃ pratijanma pracārikā /
children.translated_text: Their eldest sister, she who practiced the vow in every birth —

children.text: etatpuṇyānubhāvena sā kanyā ratisaṃnibhā // Avc_338*** //
children.translated_text: by the power of this merit, that maiden [became] beautiful as <s>Rati</s>. (338***)

children.text: dharmaśīlā vratī nāmnī dharmapattane pure vare /}
children.translated_text: Virtuous in <s>Dharma</s>, named <s>Vratī</s>, in the excellent city of <s>Dharmapattana</s>:}

children.text: tāsāṃ jyeṣṭhā pradhānā yā sā kanyā ratisaṃnibhā /
children.translated_text: She who was the eldest and foremost among them, that maiden beautiful as <s>Rati</s>,

children.text: dharmadakṣasya bhūpasya bhāryābhūd dharmacāriṇī || 339 ||
children.translated_text: became the wife of King <s>Dharmadakṣa</s>, a practitioner of the <s>Dharma</s>. (339)

children.text: tadāpi sā vratī kanyā caityasevānurāgiṇī /
children.translated_text: Even then, that maiden <s>Vratī</s>, devoted to <s>caitya</s>-worship,

children.text: saṃbodhicaraṇārāgā saṃbuddhaguṇabhāvinī || 340 ||
children.translated_text: delighting in the practice of awakening (<s>saṃbodhicaraṇa</s>), contemplating the virtues of the fully awakened one — (340)

children.text: tatra sā kanyakā sādhvī kartuṃ caityārcanaṃ mudā /
children.translated_text: there that virtuous maiden, desiring to worship the <s>caitya</s> with joy,

children.text: dharmadakṣaṃ patiṃ natvā prārthayad evam ādarāt || 341 ||
children.translated_text: bowing to her husband King <s>Dharmadakṣa</s>, prayed to him with respect thus: (341)

children.text: svāminn icchāmy ahaṃ kartuṃ caityabimbārcanaṃ sadā /
children.translated_text: 'My lord, I wish to worship the <s>caitya</s> image always,

children.text: ahorātravrataṃ cāpi tad anujñāṃ pradehi me || 342 ||
children.translated_text: and also to observe the day-and-night vow (<s>ahorātravrata</s>); please grant me permission. (342)'

children.text: iti tayā subhāvinyā bhāryayā prārthitaṃ mudā /
children.translated_text: Having heard what his good-natured wife had joyfully prayed,

children.text: śrutvā sa nṛpatir dṛṣṭvā tāṃ bhāryām evam abravīt || 343 ||
children.translated_text: that king, looking at his wife, spoke thus: (343)

children.text: bhadre sādhuḥ samicchā te yat tvayāhaṃ prabodhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'O virtuous one, excellent is your wish, by which you have awakened me;

children.text: ahaṃ cāpi cariṣyāmi tathāhorātrasadvratam || 344 ||
children.translated_text: I too shall practice the auspicious day-and-night vow. (344)'

children.text: ity uktvā sa mahīpālo dharmadakṣaḥ pramoditaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having said this, King <s>Dharmadakṣa</s>, delighted,

children.text: bhāryayā sahasaicchat tad ahorātravrataṃ varam || 345 ||
children.translated_text: together with his wife, desired to observe that excellent day-and-night vow. (345)

children.text: tataḥ sa nṛpatiś caityaṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yathāvidhi /
children.translated_text: Then that king, having established a <s>caitya</s> according to the proper rite,

children.text: ahorātravrataṃ kṛtvā sabhāryas taṃ samārcayat || 346 ||
children.translated_text: having performed the day-and-night vow, worshipped it together with his wife. (346)

children.text: evaṃ tayā subhāvinyā bhāryayā saha sarvadā /
children.translated_text: Thus, always with that good-natured wife,

children.text: dharmadakṣo narendro 'sau caityasevārato 'bhavat || 347 ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Dharmadakṣa</s>, that lord of men, became devoted to <s>caitya</s>-worship. (347)

children.text: tatas tau dampatī cāpi yāvajjīvaṃ jinārcanam /
children.translated_text: Then that couple, having performed <s>Jina</s>-worship for their entire lives,

children.text: kṛtvā saukhyaṃ prabhuktvānte saṃjagmāte jinālayam || 348 ||
children.translated_text: having enjoyed happiness, in the end went to the abode of the <s>Jina</s>. (348)

children.text: evaṃ matvātra yūyaṃ ca śraddhayā sadvrataṃ mudā /
children.translated_text: Knowing this, you too, with faith, the auspicious vow, and joy,

children.text: ahorātravrataṃ dhṛtvā bhajata caityam ādarāt || 349 ||
children.translated_text: observing the day-and-night vow, worship the <s>caitya</s> with reverence. (349)

children.text: evaṃ kṛte hi vo bhadram ihāmutra sadā bhavet /
children.translated_text: If you do thus, blessings will always be yours, here and hereafter;

children.text: kramād bodhipadaṃ prāpya gamiṣyatha jinālayam || 350 ||
children.translated_text: gradually attaining the state of awakening (<s>bodhi</s>), you will go to the abode of the <s>Jina</s>. (350)

children.text: iti śāstrā munīndreṇa samādiṣṭaṃ niśamya te /
children.translated_text: Thus, having heard what was instructed by the Teacher, the Lord of Sages,

children.text: bhikṣavo 'pi tathā caityaṃ vrataṃ dhṛtvā prabhejire || 351 ||
children.translated_text: the monks too, having observed the vow, likewise worshipped the <s>caitya</s>. (351)

children.text: evaṃ me guruṇākhyātaṃ śrutaṃ mayā narādhipa /
children.translated_text: Thus was it told to me by my teacher, and I have heard it, O lord of men;

children.text: sarvalokahitārthāya tavāpi ca pracakṣyate || 352 ||
children.translated_text: for the benefit of all the world, and for you too, it is proclaimed. (352)

children.text: tathā tvaṃ ca mahārāja saṃbodhipadalabdhaye /
children.translated_text: 'Likewise you too, O great king, for the attainment of the state of perfect awakening (<s>saṃbodhipada</s>),

children.text: ahorātravrataṃ dhṛtvā caityasevārato bhava || 353 ||
children.translated_text: upholding the day-and-night vow (<s>ahorātravrata</s>), be devoted to the worship of the <s>caitya</s> (shrine). (353)

children.text: etatpuṇyānubhāvais te sarvatra mangalaṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: 'By the power of this merit, may there be auspiciousness for you in all things;

children.text: sarvadā satsukhaṃ bhuktvā yāyāś cānte jinālayam || 354 ||
children.translated_text: having always enjoyed true happiness, may you at the end go to the abode of the <s>Jina</s> (Victor). (354)'

children.text: {E adds the following between vss. 354 and 355.
punas ca maharaja
children.translated_text: And furthermore, O great king:

children.text: dharmaṃ vinā na mokṣaṃ ca dānaṃ vinā na bhuktavān /
children.translated_text: 'Without <s>Dharma</s> there is no liberation; without giving (<s>dāna</s>) there is no enjoyment;

children.text: śrotuṃ vinā na satjñānaṃ tasmād dharmādikaṃ cara //
children.translated_text: without hearing there is no true knowledge — therefore practice <s>Dharma</s> and the rest.'
{Manuscript E adds the following between verses 354 and 355:

children.text:
saptajanmakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ tenaiva naśyate khalu /
kukṣetre ca kugotre ca jananaṃ na bhaviṣyati // Avc_354* //}
children.translated_text:
'The sins committed over seven births are indeed destroyed by this very [vow];
there will be no birth in a bad field or in a bad lineage. (354*)'}

children.text: iti tenopaguptena śāstrākhyātaṃ niśamya saḥ /
children.translated_text: Having heard from <s>Upagupta</s> what was declared by the Teacher,

children.text: aśokaḥ saprajālokas tatheti prābhyanandata || 355 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Aśoka</s>, together with his people, rejoiced saying 'So be it!' (355)

children.text: ye cedaṃ śuddhacittā jinavarakathitaṃ caityasevānubhāvam /
children.translated_text: Those who with pure minds hear or cause others to hear this account of the power of <s>caitya</s>-worship (<s>caityasevānubhāva</s>) proclaimed by the best of <s>Jinas</s>,

children.text: śṛṇvanti śrāvayanti pramuditahṛdayāḥ śraddhayābhiprasannāḥ /
children.translated_text: with delighted hearts and faith-filled serenity,

children.text: te sarvakleśamuktā jinaguṇaniratāḥ prāptasaṃbodhicittāḥ /
children.translated_text: they, freed from all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), devoted to the qualities of the <s>Jina</s>, having attained <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening),

children.text: śuddhātmānaḥ sudhīrāḥ sakalaśubhakarā buddhaloke prayānti || 356 ||
children.translated_text: pure in self, steadfastly wise, accomplishing all that is auspicious, proceed to the <s>Buddha</s>-realm. (356)

children.text: ity ahorātravratacaityasevānuśaṃsāvadānam //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the <s>Ahorātravratacaityasevānuśaṃsāvadāna</s> (Narrative of the Merits of the Day-and-Night Vow and Shrine Worship).

children.text:
{Śvadānaṃ aśokapṛcchitaṃ samāptaṃ. śubhan astu jagatāṃ.
Saṃvat 32 āśvine māse ?kṛṣṇapakṣe likha etat pam. mudā E}
children.translated_text:
{The <s>avadāna</s> requested by <s>Aśoka</s> is completed. May there be well-being for all beings.
Year 32, in the month of <s>Āśvina</s>, in the dark fortnight (?), this was copied joyfully. [Manuscript E]}
